# Precursor Behavior Identification

## 1. Overview

Precursor behaviors are lower-intensity responses that reliably precede a
higher-intensity target behavior for a given learner. Identifying them lets
staff intervene before escalation rather than after.

## 2. Identification Procedure

### 2.1 Data Collection

Collect antecedent-behavior-consequence (ABC) data across at least ten
occurrences of the target behavior. Record the full response chain leading
up to each occurrence, not just the terminal behavior.

### 2.2 Chain Analysis

Look for a response that appears in the chain across a majority of
occurrences, occurs before the target behavior with a short and consistent
latency, and is topographically distinct enough for staff to reliably detect
in the moment.

## 3. Escalation Procedure

When a precursor is detected, staff should redirect to a functionally
equivalent replacement response, prompt a previously taught coping skill,
and log the precursor occurrence separately from the target behavior in the
tracking system.

If the precursor is followed by the target behavior despite intervention,
document the attempt and escalate per the learner's individual behavior
support plan.
